songs.name: He Was A Friend Of Mine

ai_show_review.summary: Explosive Lovelight sandwich, tight Eleven and soaring Dark Star
ai_show_review.blurb: The set revolves around a massive Turn On Your Lovelight sandwich that launches into a crisp Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven sequence. Jerry’s guitar is ferocious and Phil’s bass locks in tight, while Pigpen delivers soulful vocals on He Was A Friend Of Mine. Overall the performance ranks high for its energy and tight improvisations despite occasional muddy moments.
ai_show_review.review: June 14, 1969 at the Monterey Performing Arts Center finds the Dead deep in their psychedelic stride. The first set is built around a towering Turn On Your Lovelight sandwich that segues into an inspired Dark Star → Saint Stephen → The Eleven suite, keeping the momentum blazing from start to finish. Jerry rides the high‑octane waves of The Eleven and Dark Star with possessed, nonstop runs, while Phil’s bass sparkles and ‘bombs’ through every jam. Pigpen’s raw vocal power on He Was A Friend Of Mine and his commanding presence during both Lovelight segments give the night an emotional core that balances the instrumental fireworks. The rhythm section—Mickey and Bill—provide a compact drum solo and a mid‑set break that drive the set forward, and Tom Constanten’s B3 adds a subtle, almost Vox‑like texture to the improvisations. Though the recording has occasional muddy spots and a brief dropout on Saint Stephen, it captures one of the band’s most electric 1969 performances, making it a must‑listen for anyone chasing that classic psychedelic blaze.

best_recording.reason: Solid soundboard capture of the full set with good balance; includes the complete Lovelight sandwich and Dark Star sequence despite minor dropouts.

band_performance.Billy: Keeps a tight groove alongside Mickey, reinforcing the momentum of the set.
